title: Repeatability of Low-Cost Indoor 3D Mapping: A TLS-Referenced Evaluation of Six LiDAR Odometry and Mapping Algorithms in Single- and Multi-Level Environments: code and data
description:
Evaluation pipeline, analysis scripts and run-wise results for the article Repeatability of Low-Cost Indoor 3D Mapping: A TLS-Referenced Evaluation of Six LiDAR Odometry and Mapping Algorithms in Single- and Multi-Level Environments, submitted to the Journal of Building Engineering.

Six open LiDAR–inertial SLAM algorithms — FAST-LIO2, POINT-LIO, D-LIO, HDMapping-LIO, LIO-LIVOX and the LiDAR-only baseline KISS-ICP — were run on 25 repeated handheld captures of two indoor scenarios, and every reconstruction was compared against a terrestrial laser scanning reference. The deposit contains the per-run metric tables behind every table, figure and statistical test in the article and its supplementary material, the rigid transformation of each of the 150 map–reference pairs with its RMS and inlier fraction, the element-level measurements of surface roughness, wall plumb and slab separation, and the complete code that turns one into the other.

Everything the article reports can be regenerated from what is deposited here, without access to the raw recordings.
